Pieces that carry or join CPW and coupled-trace lines: launching onto a chip, changing width, branching, bridging and coupled sections. Cross-sections that define these paths are at the end.

MTL means multi-conductor transmission line: several coupled traces that run side by side. Where a cell name says MTL, the cell holds such a set of coupled CPW traces.

## `launcher`

A tapered CPW launcher from a large pad to a CPW neck. It marks the pad-side simulation boundary.

![Default layout of `launcher`.](../../_static/images/components/launcher.svg)

Details: [Component guide](../../public-pdk-examples/components/launcher.qmd) · [Function reference](../../reference/cells.launcher.qmd)

## `taper`

A compact CPW transition between two conductor widths and gap sizes, with ports on the center-conductor DRAW layer.

![Default layout of `taper`.](../../_static/images/components/taper.svg)

Details: [Component guide](../../public-pdk-examples/components/taper.qmd)

## `cpw_t_junction`

A CPW T-junction with two trunk ports and one branch port.

![Default layout of `cpw_t_junction`.](../../_static/images/components/cpw_t_junction.svg)

Details: [Component guide](../../public-pdk-examples/components/cpw_t_junction.qmd) · [Function reference](../../reference/cells.cpw_t_junction.qmd)

## `airbridge`

A same-face airbridge: a rectangular deck with a landing via pad at each end. It has no route ports, so a parent layout places and rotates it.

![Default layout of `airbridge`.](../../_static/images/components/airbridge.svg)

Details: [Component guide](../../public-pdk-examples/components/airbridge.qmd) · [Function reference](../../reference/cells.airbridge.qmd)

## `n_trace_mtl_section`

A straight N-trace section driven by a cross-section.

![Default layout of `n_trace_mtl_section`.](../../_static/images/components/n_trace_mtl_section.svg)

Details: [Function reference](../../reference/cells.n_trace_mtl_section.qmd)

## `mtl_bend_coupling_section`

Two coupled CPW traces with four directly attached Euler bends.

![Default layout of `mtl_bend_coupling_section`.](../../_static/images/components/mtl_bend_coupling_section.svg)

Details: [Function reference](../../reference/cells.mtl_bend_coupling_section.qmd)

## `mtl_straight_bend_coupling_section`

A four-port pair around a uniform MTL section. The lower trace stays straight; the upper trace leaves each side through a 90-degree Euler bend.

![Default layout of `mtl_straight_bend_coupling_section`.](../../_static/images/components/mtl_straight_bend_coupling_section.svg)

Details: [Function reference](../../reference/cells.mtl_straight_bend_coupling_section.qmd)

## `mtl_straight_bend_transition`

A four-port transition from an MTL seam to a straight trace and a bend.

![Default layout of `mtl_straight_bend_transition`.](../../_static/images/components/mtl_straight_bend_transition.svg)

Details: [Function reference](../../reference/cells.mtl_straight_bend_transition.qmd)

## `mtl_bend_bend_transition`

A four-port transition from an MTL seam to two opposing bends.

![Default layout of `mtl_bend_bend_transition`.](../../_static/images/components/mtl_bend_bend_transition.svg)

Details: [Function reference](../../reference/cells.mtl_bend_bend_transition.qmd)

## Cross-sections {#cross-sections}

Choose a registered cross-section to define widths, transverse offsets, layers and connection ports along a path. Browse the [Cross-sections guide](../../public-pdk-examples/cross-sections.qmd) for the registered choices and their default previews.
